description: Linear programming, simplex method, sensitivity analysis, transportation problems, network flow, integer programming.
Unix systems, network programming, object-oriented programming, applications in Industrial Engineering.
Non-linear programming, dynamic programming, queuing theory, Markov chains, optimization techniques.
Manufacturing systems, concurrent engineering, robotics, CNC, process planning, MRP, JIT systems, flexible manufacturing systems.
Use of OR software like LINDO and LINGO for solving linear programming problems and mini projects.
Ergonomics, anthropometry, manual handling, work measurement, job evaluation, productivity and work design.
Probability theory, random variables, distributions, sampling theory, estimation, hypothesis testing.

Engineering economy concepts including time value of money, present worth, rate of return, replacement analysis, and project evaluation. Basics of accounting including financial statements and double entry bookkeeping. Costing concepts including material, labour, overheads, job costing, process costing, marginal and standard costing, and cost control.

prerequisite: Introduction to Engineering Practice or Equivalent
description: Hands-on training in machining, CNC operations, EDM, grinding, measurement techniques, foundry processes, and welding practices including gas welding, MIG, and submerged arc welding.

Quality management concepts including TQM, ISO standards, statistical process control, control charts, acceptance sampling, reliability analysis, maintenance, and design of experiments including Taguchi methods.
Experiments on quality control including control charts, sampling plans, workflow systems, life testing, and online quality monitoring.

Concepts of logistics and supply chain including facility location, transportation, inventory management, procurement, coordination strategies, bullwhip effect, global supply chains, and performance measurement.
Experimental design and analysis including ANOVA, factorial designs, response surface methodology, Taguchi methods, orthogonal arrays, and parameter design.
Discrete and continuous simulation techniques including random number generation, simulation modeling, statistical analysis, optimization, and validation of simulation systems.
Advanced optimization techniques including genetic algorithms, neural networks, fuzzy optimization, simulated annealing, data envelopment analysis, and evolutionary computing.
Machine tools and machining processes including CNC machines, tool geometry, chip formation, cutting temperature, tool wear, machining economics, and advanced machining techniques.
Project-based application of optimization techniques such as genetic algorithms, neural networks, fuzzy logic, simulated annealing, and evolutionary computing.
